text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eleven police officers to stand trial for the December 18 murder of two Kenyatta University students.
- Legislator Stephen Ndicho is freed after the High Court substituted a 5,000-shilling fine for a six-month jail term.
- The government denies knowledge of plans to import uncertified powdered milk.
- Kisumu airport is closed after fire destroys navigational aids.
- The chairman of opposition FORD-Asili party proposes a meeting jetween President Daniel arap Moi and opposition leaders.
- Ford Motor Company announces it is returning to the Kenyan market and has chosen Lonrho Motors as its partner.
- President Moi warns aliens against causing chaos in the country.
- Education minister Joseph Kamotho says the drop-out rate of girls from school due to unwanted pregnancies is alarming.
- The Central Organisation of Trade Unions and the Kenya Consumer Organisation call for legislation to control frequent oil hikes. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
